subject: Deckard: migration safety checks and activation timeline
messages:
From: Avery Smith <avery.smith@deckard.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deckard migration: activation timeline & capacity ask

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. We're locking down our internal go-live window and wanted to share a short matrix with expected traffic and a proposed activation timeline so Redwood can validate capacity and acceptance gates. Attached: deckard_migration_matrix.xlsx (traffic by endpoint, QPS, avg tokens), sla_draft_2026-09-14.pdf.

A few highlights:
- Expected sustained peak: 250 rps across 4 endpoints (text-gen/chat/embed) with median response sizes ~180 tokens and occasional spikes to 800 tokens.
- KV cache benefits expected for chat history on user-facing flows — we'll provide a sample prefix distribution.
- Target activation window: 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-07 (primary) with a warm-up week starting 2026-09-28.

Asks:
1) Can your infra/ops confirm a GPU fleet plan (counts + instance types) that hits <150ms p95 for the primary traffic profile?
2) Can we schedule a 60-minute validation run with the ops team next week?
3) Any immediate redlines on the attached SLA? Procurement will need details for PO timing.

Thanks — appreciate the help.

— Avery

I'll propose a few slots for the validation run: Thu 9/16 10:00 PT or Mon 9/20 14:00 PT — ping me which works.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deckard migration: activation timeline & capacity ask

Hi all — attaching a small kv_cache_profile.png that shows the type of prefix hit distribution we expect to see (high reuse in support flows, low reuse in ad-hoc generation). Preliminary capacity guidance based on the supplied matrix:

- Baseline assumption: 250 rps sustained -> ~6x concurrency at 40ms per-token backend for short responses; for long-tail 800-token responses we need to provision for concurrent KV loads.
- Recommended initial dedicated fleet: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) with a 2-GPU hot pool for spillover. This assumes int8 quantization options enabled and continuous batching set to conservative latency SLOs.
- If Deckard wants to keep hosted-to-dedicated routing with graceful fallback, we should provision an additional 2x lower-cost GPUs (for cheaper model variant) in the warm-up period.

Action items for Deckard: please upload the real prefix distribution sample and a 24-hour synthetic traffic dump (timestamps + tokens) — we can run a quick validation script to produce expected p95/p99 latency curves.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi team — quick updates:

- Procurement: Billing contact is Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@deckard.ai>. We can sign the SLA (with the two proposed clarifications) by 2026-09-21.
- Technical: attaching the prefix sample and a 24hr synthetic trace (shared to the Drive link). We expect KV hit-rate ~62% on support flows and ~18% across casual chat.
- Acceptance gates proposed:
  * smoke test (5m QPS synthetic) with p95 < 220ms
  * ramp test 50% traffic for 2 hours with <2% error rate
  * final cut to 100% with staged rollback windows (15m, 60m)

We can target the validation run on Mon 9/20 14:00 PT. For the go-live, Deckard prefers 2026-10-05 00:00 PT start of warm-up.

Thanks — Avery
